newsitem.title: USA: Telebras falls on currency fears, profit-take.
newsitem.headline: Telebras falls on currency fears, profit-take.

text.p: High-flying Brazilian telephone holding Telebras SA tumbled in early trade Tuesday, hit by profit-taking and currency jitters, traders and analysts said.

Telebras American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) were off 10-1/2 to 135-3/4 in heavy volume. The ADRs were the fifth most-active issue on the New York Stock Exchange and also among the exchange's leading percentage losers.

Traders and analysts said Telebras had been weighed down in part by rumors that Brazil would devalue its currency and by profit-taking after a strong run. Telebras, a darling among investors, has risen from 76.50 at the end of 1996, and hit a high of 169 Thursday.
"The worst rumor is devaluation after what's happened in the Far East markets," said Ray Kelly, Latin America director at Robert Fleming.
The Malaysian ringgit is the latest Southeast Asian currency to come under speculative attack. Some investors fear Brazil, with its persistent trade deficit, could also come under pressure.

"There is also a lot of crowd mentality -- 'I've made a 50 percent profit, I'd better lock something in'," Kelly said. "Even at these levels, there is a lot of profit" in Telebras and other Brazilian telecommunications stocks.
Despite the drop in the ADR price, UBS Securities analyst Mickey Schleien repeated his strong buy rating for Telebras. Lehman Brothers analyst Matthew Hickman also reiterated his buy recommendation.
Hickman raised his 12-month price target for the ADRs to $175 from 135.
"In technical terms, the correction was long overdue," he said. "It's done very well, but there is strong fundamental value."
Traders and analysts also said Telebras had been hit by fears of competition as Brazil privatizes its telephone sector and as Brazilian mutual funds pull out of the local markets.
In Sao Paulo, Telebras preferred was down six reais at 152. Telebras preferred is the benchmark stock of the Sao Paulo Exchange and the underlying issue of the ADRs.
Telebras common was down 6.01 reais at 136.01.
